# Legacy Codex CI adapter

Required adaptation for this authorized personal-fork experiment only. Original deterministic stage/manifest/binding/slices/perf scripts and verdict/status/artifact contracts are retained. Original plan body is extracted without behavioral changes into legacy-plan.ts for Node24 native TypeScript execution. Original prompts are retained in legacy-runner/src/prompts and rendered into legacy-prompts.md. DSH event prompts become conditional static guidance; this is an explicit event-routing adaptation, not an assertion that Codex supports DSH events.

Official codex-cli 0.155.1 supports --ignore-user-config (verified in local exec --help). Existing ChatGPT login is used with requested gpt-6.1-sol and provider openai. No DeepSeek, relay or paid API key is used. The host preserves JSONL events, exact final report, CLI exitCode and session metadata/usage. Requested fields are not actual model evidence; runtime session metadata is checked independently and missing/mismatched identity prevents PASS.

bbdev-mcp.py adds the original deterministic plan to the same real bbdev FastMCP process that submits and polls trace_ids. Compiler/workload/BEMU/RTL operations retain bbdev execution semantics. Config install alone uses the actual CLI. Missing exact tool equivalence is INFRA.

Negative tests must not enter ordinary pass-required stems. A separate expected-failure manifest and backend run requires terminal failure, nonzero simulation returncode, matching task/binary identity and explicit expected panic/assert text in trace-bound logs. Build/network/tool failure, missing logs or cancellation cannot satisfy a negative. Old manifest had no expected-failure semantics; this is an explicitly recorded engineering completion rather than a changed normal gate.

## Optional C API compiler gate

An explicit `cApiCompilerCheck` object admits the frozen Clamp fixture suite; exact schema is saved in experiment evidence `manifests/c-api-extension-spec.json`. It is absent from original round 1 and does not change that round. The real MCP tool `buckyball_c_api_compiler_check` uses current source HEAD, verifies tracked fixture/API/generator inputs are unchanged, regenerates params.h and ballISA.h through the canonical Chip.pb generator, and resolves the actual RISC-V GCC/G++ executables. Four GNU C11/C++17 O0/O2 positive objects must be successful real RISC-V ELF objects. All 12 CASEs in all four modes (48 compiles) must exit nonzero with the BB_CLAMP_STATIC_CHECK negative-array-size diagnostic. Missing headers/tools, unrelated errors, signals and compiler crashes are INFRA; accepted illegal values are FAIL.

The host audit records exact SHA, arguments, UTC timestamps, compiler target/version/binary hashes, source/header hashes, object hashes, and individual stdout/stderr log hashes and exit codes. The terminal gate rejects missing/duplicate matrix cells and mismatched source SHA. Matrix files and logs are archived beneath codex-session-evidence/c-api-compiler-check by the existing session artifact. Static admission tests are synthetic, clearly marked, and are not compiler execution evidence.

The workflow must set `BB_VERIFY_CODEX_BIN` to the absolute executable path of the authorized official CLI release. Missing or non-executable paths fail closed as INFRA before config/build work. The adapter records the resolved binary path, SHA-256, actual `--version` output and exit code in `codex-binary.json`; session archive compares actual `session_meta.cli_version` to that probed version, separately from actual turn model and provider. The experiment uses the verified official 0.162.1 release; 0.155.1 rejected this model on the same ChatGPT account. Matching code-mode-host installation is managed by the workflow host, without changing account config or auth.

## Bounded status diagnostics and report preservation

Every native status response remains complete in the audit and a SHA-256 addressed JSON file under `codex-session-evidence/native-status`. Only oversized diagnostic strings in the model-facing copy are shortened, with first diagnostic, leading/trailing excerpts and original absolute path/hash/field metadata. Control fields and ordinary body fields remain unchanged; trusted negative checks consume the full native response.

CLI final output goes to `codex-final.md`. An already written `report.md` remains intact; only a missing report is populated from final output. A disagreement between first-line verdicts is INFRA. Both files are archived with session evidence; report gates and identity checks still apply.

## Genuine Boost runtime preflight

Before starting bbdev, the adapter verifies the installed `libboost-system1.83.0:amd64` source, exact `libboost_system.so.1.83.0` SONAME and SHA-256, and copies only that regular library into a private session-evidence directory. It supplies only this directory as `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to the same MCP process and its project Nix children. No whole system library path or alternate-version SONAME link is used. For an existing BEMU ELF, its actual Nix interpreter must resolve the complete dependency graph and the private Boost copy through `--list`; missing BEMU is recorded as not yet proved, with formal build/simulation still required. Commands, hashes and loader output are retained under `codex-session-evidence/runtime-closure/preflight.json`. This is dependency evidence, never a functional PASS.
